title: Finite-coefficient proper direct image on the localizing categories
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$. All schemes below are separated and of finite type over $k$, and all arrows are $k$-morphisms, in the standing setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting, def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring with $\ell^n1_A=0$ for some $n\geq1$, and let $p:X\to Y$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Use ordinary module sheaves over the constant discrete ring $A$ on the small étale and pro-étale sites and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. The coefficient identifications [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-condensed-ring-constant, lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-scheme-ring-constant] identify these with module objects over the pulled-back condensed finite ring. Write $\Dctf(T,A)$ for bounded complexes with constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude [sk-def-sfb-constructible]: there exist integers $a\leq b$ such that $\mathcal H^r(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N[0])=0$ for every module sheaf $N$ and every $r\notin[a,b]$. Write $\Loc(\Dctf(T,A))$ for its smallest full replete triangulated closure under all small ambient coproducts [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Use the total K-injective derived pushforward $Rp_*$ and the exact inverse image $g^*$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Then:

1. $Rp_*$ maps $\Dctf(X,A)$ into $\Dctf(Y,A)$ and restricts to an exact functor $\Loc(\Dctf(X,A))\to\Loc(\Dctf(Y,A))$ preserving arbitrary small direct sums.
2. For a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with $X'=X\times_Y Y'$, projections $p':X'\to Y'$ and $g':X'\to X$, and $g:Y'\to Y$, the canonical map $\beta_K:g^*Rp_*K\to Rp'_*g'^*K$ is an isomorphism for every $K\in\Loc(\Dctf(X,A))$. Here $Y'$ and $X'$ are also in the standing setting, and $\beta_K$ is the adjunction mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] of $p'^*g^*Rp_*K\simeq g'^*p^*Rp_*K\xrightarrow{g'^*\varepsilon_p}g'^*K$.
3. For an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-open-immersion], extension by zero $j_!$ [sk-def-sfb-finite-lower-shriek] preserves $\Dctf(-,A)$ and arbitrary small sums and restricts to an exact sum-preserving functor on these localizing categories. Consequently, for any chosen compactification $f=p\circ j$ within the standing setting, with $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ open and $p:X\to Y$ proper, $Rp_*j_!$ maps $\Dctf(U,A)$ into $\Dctf(Y,A)$ and restricts to an exact sum-preserving functor $\Loc(\Dctf(U,A))\to\Loc(\Dctf(Y,A))$.

proof.text: Each standing scheme is Noetherian and qcqs: a field is Noetherian, then apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. A finite ring is Noetherian by the ascending chain condition on its finite ideal set. The two finite-discrete coefficient lemmas identify its condensed pullback with constant $A$. Hence [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] identifies the étale and pro-étale Dctf subcategories. Obtain $e$ and the uniform geometric bound from [lem-sfb-finite-proper-geometric-cd-bound], and classicality of the localizing closure from [lem-sfb-finite-classical-localizing].

The bound $2e$ allows [det-ctf-finite-proper-tor] to send an étale $C$ of Tor interval $[a,b]$ into the small target category with interval $[a,b+2e]$. Proper maps are qcqs (finite type and [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]). The bounded-below comparison [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] identifies $Rp_*\nu_X^*C$ with $\nu_Y^*Rp_{\mathrm{ét},*}C$. Thus $Rp_*$ preserves the small subcategory.

source.place: Étale statements and Transfer: preservation of generators

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-finite-proper-classical-coproducts], $Rp_*$ preserves sums of classical complexes. It is triangulated by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. Therefore the classical objects sent into $\Loc(\Dctf(Y,A))$ form a replete triangulated subcategory closed under ambient sums and containing $\Dctf(X,A)$. Minimality [sk-def-localizing-closure] gives preservation of its closure. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-triangulated-functor-restriction] for the exact restriction, proving (1).

For (2), fix $m$ and set $N=m-2e-2$. The canonical mate [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange] is natural for $K\to\tau_{\geq N}K$. Its left vertical map is invertible in degree $m$ by [lem-sfb-finite-proper-classical-truncation] and exact $g^*$. The right one is invertible by the same lemma after base change: [lem-sfb-finite-classical-localizing] makes $g'^*K$ classical, and exact pullback commutes with truncation. The bottom mate is invertible by [sk-thm-properbasechange], since its input is bounded below and its underlying cohomology is killed by $\ell^n$. This theorem's exchange is the same unit--square--counit mate. Hence $\mathcal H^m\beta_K$ is invertible for every $m$, proving (2).

source.place: Étale statements: bounded-below proper base change and naturality

proof.text: Apply [det-proper-image-localizing-open] to the admissible coefficient $A$ with its discrete topology. It gives all open assertions in (3). For a compactification compose its exact sum-preserving restriction with that of (1). The two canonical coproduct comparisons compose, preserving each coprojection, so the composite preserves sums and the small subcategory, including the empty family.

The item statement and stmt_deps are byte-identical to the live node. The 17-step, 15,969-character proof is now a 5-step assembly of about 2,600 characters. Mapping of old steps: 1→new step 1. 2→lem-sfb-finite-proper-geometric-cd-bound plus new step 2 (det-ctf-finite-proper-tor with d=2e). 3→new step 2. 4→lem-sfb-finite-classical-localizing. 5–10→lem-sfb-finite-proper-classical-truncation, stated for every S→Y, which covers both old 9 and old 10. 11–12→lem-sfb-finite-proper-classical-coproducts. 13→new step 3. 14→the existing sk-thm-properbasechange: I read its statement and its 9 proof steps, and it states exactly the D^+_class proét exchange with torsion cohomology, for the def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange mate, via the same classical-equivalence, forget and transport argument. The blueprint proof also cites it here. 15→new step 4. 16–17→new step 5. The four new nodes are statement-only, unsplit, with created.item set and source pointing to main-20261015. The preflight requires this; the drafts are kept in the report. I checked each new node for truth: the fibre bound after base change (0A3V and fibre-dimension invariance) and the geometric torsion cd ≤ 2e with cd(Ω)=0; closure of classical cohomology (BS weak Serre, exact Grothendieck sums, pullback commuting with ν*, Dctf classical for qcqs T); the truncation window (095U relative cd 2e after any base change; the cone τ≤N−1 needs N<m−2e+1, and the node requires the stronger N<m−2e−1); and the coproducts (qcqs bounded-below continuity plus the window, empty family included). Small cases e=0 and empty fibres hold. I checked every item hypothesis: Y quasi-compact, d=2e covering ℓ-power torsion, the S=Y and S=Y' uses of the truncation node, τ≥N K bounded below, classical and killed by ℓ^n for sk-thm-properbasechange, and finite ℓ-power A admissible for det-proper-image-localizing-open. None of the 4 new nodes duplicates an existing one: I compared lem-amb-proper-coproducts (étale, Noetherian), lem-sfb-adic-proper-bounded-below-coproducts, det-proper-unbounded-window-ii-general, det-pe-unbounded-classical-truncation, lem-sfb-unbounded-direct-image-truncation-stability, lem-exc-finite-cd-derived-coproduct-criterion, lem-weil-pbc-proetale-module-cohomology-coproducts and lem-kun/cbc/fin fibre-bound nodes. The reached node lem-pod-lisse-module-sheaves-as-module-objects is a generic lisse/FLC module-object equivalence. The base step 14 already reached it through thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below. I recomputed the closures: both contain 32 trf/pod nodes, and the delivery adds none. There is no SGA citation.
